stem: A retailer's legacy-systems team wants to move an existing on-premises Java application into Amazon ECS containers without changing the application's source code.

choices.text: Deploy the application to Amazon EKS using a Kubernetes manifest the team writes
Rewrite the application as a set of AWS Lambda functions
Use AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) to rehost the application on a new EC2 instance without containerizing it
Use AWS App2Container to analyze the running application and generate the container image and ECS task definition

rationale: AWS App2Container analyzes an application already running on a server, identifies its runtime and dependencies, packages it into a container image, and generates the ECS task definition, all without requiring source code changes, which is exactly the lift-and-shift the team wants. Amazon EKS runs Kubernetes, not the Amazon ECS target the team chose, and a hand-written manifest still needs a container image that nothing in this option builds from the running server. AWS Application Migration Service rehosts a server onto a new EC2 instance as a lift-and-shift migration, but it does not produce a container image or an ECS task definition, so the application ends up on EC2, not in a container. Rewriting the application as a set of Lambda functions changes its source code, which the team explicitly wants to avoid, and does not put it into ECS containers.
